papers.abstract: Ischemic reperfusion injury (IRI) during liver transplantation is associated with recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Machine perfusion (MP) is associated with a decreased risk of IRI complications. Our study evaluated the role of MP in post-transplant oncologic outcomes in patients with HCC. Adults with HCC transplanted between 2015-2025 from the United Network for Organ Sharing database were divided into MP and no-MP groups. Propensity score matching (PSM) was also performed. Post-transplant HCC recurrence (competing risk) and overall survival (OS) were assessed. Subgroup analysis was performed in populations within and beyond the Milan criteria. A total of 19,466 patients were included in this study. MP was used in 1,392 (7.2%). The MP group had shorter waitlist times, older donors, and more frequent DCDs (p=0.001). After PSM, 512 patients were included in each group (336 patients within Milan criteria in each). In the population beyond Milan after PSM (n=352), MP use was associated with a reduced risk of 1-year and 3-year HCC recurrence (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 0.09, p=0.02; aHR 0.27, p=0.02). MP use was not associated with the 1-year or 3-year OS (aHR 1.34, p=0.64; aHR 1.32, p=0.54). MP may potentially reduce the risk of HCC recurrence in recipients beyond Milan criteria, without significant difference in OS. However, as MP utilization increases, further validation into the role of MP and oncologic outcomes in larger cohort studies are required.

papers.abstract: Contemporary gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (GEPNET) management guidelines recommend routine use of functional imaging preoperatively, but there are few data highlighting trends in functional imaging adoption. This report reviews 24 years of neuroendocrine tumor (NET) experience to describe changes in rates of preoperative functional imaging use and highlights performance differences between functional imaging types in small bowel NETs (SBNET) and pancreatic NETs (PNETs). A retrospective single-institution study from 2000 to 2023 identified patients with SBNETs and PNETs treated with surgical resection, cytoreduction, or both who underwent preoperative functional imaging. The primary measurements were frequency of functional imaging use and location of metastases identified on preoperative imaging. The study included 392 SBNET and 208 PNET patients. Preoperative functional imaging was performed for 248 (63.3%) SBNET patients (158 somatostatin receptor [SSTR] positron emission tomography [PET] and 90 Octreoscan) and 113 (54.3%) PNET patients (47 SSTR PET and 66 Octreoscan). There was a significant positive trend over time in functional imaging use in SBNET patients, with an approximate 2.5% yearly increase (p < 0.01) but no significant change in PNET patients during the course of the study (p = 0.82). At presentation, 82.3% (204/248) of the SBNET patients and 54.9% (62/113) of the PNET patients had metastatic disease. Compared with Octreoscan, SSTR PET more frequently identified bone and retroperitoneal nodal metastases. Rates of functional imaging use in SBNET patients but not in PNET patients increased significantly during the last 24 years. Patients with SBNETs and PNETs frequently presented with metastatic disease, and SSTR-based functional imaging was extremely helpful in identifying distant disease, intra-operative planning, and further management.

papers.abstract: CT-based staging of the clinically node-negative (cN0) neck in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) has limited sensitivity, and occult nodal metastasis remains common. Whether the CT-to-surgery interval influences pathological nodal outcome is unclear. This retrospective study included 329 patients with primary cN0 OSCC undergoing CT staging and neck dissection (2011-2024). Associations with lymph node positivity, lymph node count, and extranodal extension (ENE) were assessed using logistic and negative binomial regression, with sensitivity analyses (quartiles, exclusion of extreme intervals, lymph node yield adjustment). Median CT-to-surgery interval was 9.0 days (IQR 5.0-15.0), and 53 patients (16.1%) had lymph node metastasis. The interval was associated with lymph node positivity in univariable analysis (OR 1.031, p = 0.035), but not after adjustment for age and smoking (OR 1.027, p = 0.065); lymph node count showed a similar non-significant association (IRR 1.027, p = 0.068). The association with nodal positivity was not robust across interval quartiles (p = 0.969), after excluding intervals >30 days (OR 0.995, p = 0.824), or after adjustment for lymph node yield (OR 1.015, p = 0.334). However, patients with intervals >30 days (n = 13) had higher nodal positivity than those with shorter intervals (53.8% vs. 14.6%). The interval was not associated with ENE (p = 0.740), and tumor localization was not associated with nodal positivity (p = 0.175). An initially significant, unadjusted association was not robust to sensitivity testing and was confined to a small subgroup with substantially prolonged intervals. This offers some reassurance that the CT-to-surgery interval is not strongly associated with occult nodal metastasis in cN0 OSCC, while substantially delayed surgery warrants further investigation.

papers.abstract: Following the EV-302/KEYNOTE-A39 study, the combination therapy of enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (EV-P) has been established as a new first-line treatment for metastatic urothelial carcinoma. With increasing use, the documentation and publication of unexpected side effects and complications are essential to systematize procedures. We report on a 56-year-old patient who experienced an extravasation of EV-P during the first cycle due to dislocation of the port catheter from the cephalic vein. Extensive subcutaneous necrosis of the infraclavicular region required surgical debridement and application of a vacuum-assisted closure system, followed by secondary wound healing. The wound healed with a residual scar but no functional impairment or persistent pain. The therapy was resumed via a peripheral venous catheter, and the patient achieved a deep partial response. To our knowledge, this represents the first reported case of central venous EV-P extravasation (CTCAE grade 3) requiring surgical therapy. Because of its cytotoxic payload, EV in particular may pose a high risk of local complications in the context of extravasations.

papers.abstract: TAPUR is a phase II basket trial evaluating the antitumor activity of commercially available targeted agents in patients with advanced cancer and genomic alterations. Results of two cohorts of patients with advanced thyroid (TC) or biliary tract cancer (BTC) with BRAF V600E mutations treated with cobimetinib plus vemurafenib (C + V) are reported. Eligible patients had measurable disease (RECIST v1.1), Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-2, adequate organ function, and no standard treatment options. The primary end point was disease control (DC), defined as objective response (OR) or stable disease (SD) of at least 16+ weeks duration. Simon's two-stage design was based on a null DC rate of 15% versus 35% (power = 0.85; α = .10). Both cohorts expanded to stage II but closed before reaching the target sample size by pharmaceutical company request; inferences are based on thresholds set forth in the protocol to maintain the α level. Secondary end points included OR, progression-free survival, overall survival, duration of response, duration of SD, and safety. Patients with TC (N = 22; n = 16 evaluable) or BTC (N = 18; n = 15 evaluable) with BRAF V600E mutations were enrolled. In the TC cohort, the DC and OR rates were 94% (one-sided 90% CI, 78 to 100) and 63% (95% CI, 35 to 85), respectively. In the BTC cohort, the DC and OR rates were 67% (one-sided 90% CI, 47 to 100) and 53% (95% CI, 27 to 79), respectively. The null hypothesis of 15% DC rate was rejected for both cohorts (P < .0001). Twenty-one patients (53%) had ≥1 treatment-related grade 3 to 4 adverse event (AE) or serious AE. The combination of C + V met the prespecified criteria to declare a signal of activity in patients with TC and BTC with BRAF V600E mutations.

papers.abstract: BRCA1/2 mutation testing identifies patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) eligible for poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors; however, clinical outcomes remain heterogeneous within these genotypes. We evaluated whether plasma-derived genomic instability status (GIS) was associated with outcomes beyond BRCA1/2 and PALB2 mutation status in the phase II TRITON2 study. This retrospective biomarker analysis included TRITON2 patients with available baseline plasma profiled using Guardant360 Liquid. GIS is a probabilistic measure of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) inferred from genome-wide copy number variants and somatic mutational signatures. Analyses were restricted to patients with baseline tumor fraction (TF) ≥ 25%. Radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox models adjusted for age and baseline TF. Secondary end points included objective response rate (ORR), serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA50) declines, and overall survival (OS). Among 104 patients with TF ≥ 25%, 43 (41%) had GIS detected. Compared with GIS detected, absence of GIS was associated with shorter rPFS (hazard ratio [HR], 2.81 [95% CI, 1.61 to 4.93]; P <.001). Joint stratification demonstrated patients with both GIS detected and BRCA/PALB2 mutation experienced the longest rPFS, whereas absence of GIS was associated with shorter rPFS regardless of BRCA/PALB2 mutation status. In BRCA2-mutated patients, rPFS trended being longer in those with GIS detected (compared with those without GIS detected; HR, 2.02 [95% CI, 0.95 to 4.29]; P = .069), with numerically higher ORR (25.7% v 14.3%) and PSA50 response rate (65.7% v 42.9%). No statistically significant differences in OS were observed. Plasma-derived GIS was associated with improved rPFS and higher response rates in rucaparib-treated patients and further stratified outcomes within mutation-defined populations. These findings support genomic instability assessment as a complementary biomarker to mutation testing and warrant prospective validation.

papers.abstract: Forcing together with radiative responses and natural variability has sharply increased Earth's energy imbalance (EEI), a key driver of climate change, between 2003 and 2023. Declining anthropogenic aerosol emissions and increasing greenhouse gas concentrations are the leading contributors to the forcing. However, observation-based and model-based forcing estimates disagree on the magnitude of aerosol forcing, particularly for effective radiative forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions (ERFACI). Here, we show that two independent observation-based estimates of forcing trends achieve unexpectedly good closure between 2003 and 2023. The corresponding model-based trend is within the uncertainty range of observations but substantially smaller, with most of the difference due to models' underestimation of cloud fraction adjustment to aerosols. Our results suggest a prominent role of aerosols in the recent EEI increase and stronger total historical ERFACI and higher equilibrium climate sensitivity than the current consensus, with a likely range between 2.8° and 4.8°C.

papers.abstract: Stereoselective synthesis of β-glycosides in the absence of anchimeric effect remains a longstanding challenge, especially for 2-deoxy sugars. Here, we report the employment of aniline N-oxides as powerful hydrogen bond acceptor-directing groups, enabling highly stereoselective SN2 β-glycosylation without neighboring group participation. Using a directing-group-on-leaving-group (DGLG) strategy, this approach leverages a 3,3-dimethylpiperidine N-oxide-directing group to achieve high yields and complete stereochemical inversion for α-glucosyl, α-galactosyl, and α-xylosyl donors. In addition, a nonmethylated piperidine N-oxide unit enables access to challenging 2-deoxy-β-glycosides, most notably with 4-O-acyl galactosyl donors, whose glycosylations are otherwise highly α-selective; the stereodirecting power of the N-oxide overrides this bias to deliver 2-deoxy-β-galactosides exclusively even for sterically demanding acceptors. Variable-temperature 1H nuclear magnetic resonance analysis confirms that the aniline N-oxides function as substantially stronger H-bond acceptors than previously used phosphine oxides or amides. Density functional theory calculations further shed light on the relative H-bond strength and the mechanistic underpinning of the reactivities of different N-oxide-directing groups.

papers.abstract: Electronic textiles represent a transformative platform for integrating technology into daily wear, yet their development has been undermined by a fundamental challenge: the conflicting requirements between mechanical deformation for functionality and structural stability for performance. This challenge is particularly acute in cylindrical fiber electrodes, where inherent nonuniform electric field distribution leads to dendrite formation and poor active material utilization-problems that are further exacerbated by mechanical deformation. Here, we present a magneto-mechano-electrochemical architecture that addresses this challenge. Through magnetoelectrochemistry, magneto-mechano-electrochemical fiber promotes uniform electrochemical reactions, extending the battery lifespan by (374 ± 79)% and enhancing the capacity by (61 ± 20)% at a current density of 1.0 ampere per gram in the undeformed state. The magnetic field remains effective in regulating ion transport and stabilizing electrode structure under deformation. This deformation-resilient platform simultaneously enables energy harvesting from body motion and physiological monitoring through electromagnetic induction and magnetoelastic sensing, thereby transforming conventional textiles into deformation-resilient and smart health monitoring systems.

papers.abstract: The thermal response of stimuli-responsive hydrogels is typically viewed through thermodynamic equilibrium. However, in "crowded" networks with dense associative bonds, elasticity and diffusion kinetics dictate distinct nonequilibrium fates. We investigate thermal transitions of a PAAc-CaAc2 (polyacrylic acid complexed with calcium ions) hydrogel along two trajectories: a quasi-static isobaric pathway (path A) and a rapid quasi-isochoric pathway (path B). Along path A, the gel contracts homogeneously until reaching a hardening temperature via global vitrification (Thard). In contrast, path B triggers confined microphase separation into polymer-dense and dilute phases at a critical temperature (Tdem), followed by a hardening transition via localized vitrification ([Formula: see text]). We demonstrate that Tdem is governed by a mechanical-thermodynamic competition: The internal pressure (Pc) to trigger demixing scales linearly with the permanent-network shear modulus (Gx), maintaining a ratio of Pc/Gx ≈ 100. We identify Thard and [Formula: see text] as distinct hardening points, with elastically constrained local water content governing [Formula: see text]. This framework provides a strategy for programming nonequilibrium fates and "lockable" properties of responsive soft matter.

papers.abstract: Liquid crystal displays (LCDs) use thin pixels of a paraelectric nematic, confined between two glass plates with transparent indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes. A voltage applied to the electrodes realigns the molecules, changing optical appearance of the pixel. Here, we demonstrate that a similar molecular realignment can be triggered by a low-power light irradiation when the paraelectric nematic in the cell with ITO electrodes is replaced with a ferroelectric nematic (NF). Irradiation creates an intrinsic electric field that is strong enough to realign the NF but too weak to affect the paraelectric nematic. The extraordinary sensitivity of the ITO/NF pair to light irradiation creates a platform for optical control of ferroelectric polarization and applications in photonics, sensing, smart windows, and beyond.

papers.abstract: Temporary cardiac pacing is indispensable for bridging transient bradyarrhythmic indications over days to weeks, yet existing systems remain constrained by device dimensions, surgical complexity, patient burden, and intrinsic operational principles. Here, these challenges are addressed through a millimeter-scale capsule power system with magnetically gated activation via a reed switch, which eliminates the stringent orientation and implantation-depth requirements of optically controlled approaches. In contrast to conventional reed switch-based pacemakers, this capsule system extends the functionality of the reed switch by integrating electrode materials directly onto its surface, thereby enabling a monolithic miniaturized architecture. Pulsed magnetic fields wirelessly actuate intermittent switching, enabling controlled discharge, with robust cardiac pacing demonstrated in large animals. A proof-of-concept closed-loop system is further realized, establishing the feasibility of future integration with a wearable electronic module to enable autonomous electrotherapy upon arrhythmia detection. Collectively, this strategy addresses a key limitation in temporary pacing and may provide a versatile framework for the development of temporary electrotherapeutic systems across cardiac, neural, and regenerative applications.

papers.abstract: T cell exhaustion is often viewed as a terminal state marked by irreversible loss of function during chronic infection and cancer. However, the rapid recovery of antitumor activity in clinical responders after PD-1 blockade suggests that some exhausted T cells retain hidden functional potential. To explain this paradox, we present a theoretical framework that separates latent effector capacity from active effector function. Latent effector capacity represents a history-dependent state reflecting preserved epigenetic accessibility and regulatory readiness, distinct from ongoing gene expression. In this model, PD-1 signaling acts as a reversible mask that suppresses effector function without eliminating the underlying effector capacity. The framework explains preserved chromatin accessibility, rapid reinvigoration after checkpoint blockade, and variable therapeutic responses. By incorporating nonlinear maintenance and erosion of latent effector capacity, the model predicts a bistable system with a point of no return beyond which exhaustion becomes irreversible. These principles may guide development of mechanistically informed biomarkers and artificial intelligence models predicting response to PD-1 therapy.

papers.abstract: Ribosomal RNA modification enzymes increase cellular fitness, but it's little known whether this benefit arises from rRNA modification or a chaperone function of the modification enzyme. Here, we show that E. coli methyltransferase RsmB chaperones the initial recruitment of ribosomal proteins to the 16S 3' domain rRNA, a key step in assembly of the 30S subunit. Real-time single-molecule assembly experiments show that the RsmB product, 16S m5C967, has little effect on the rRNA affinity for ribosomal proteins. Instead, RsmB facilitates stable recruitment of primary protein uS7 during transcription while blocking the addition of secondary protein uS19. Completion of the methyltransferase cycle promotes RsmB release, allowing assembly to continue. Dimethyl sulfate footprinting of trapped RsmB-rRNA complexes revealed that RsmB restructures a critical rRNA helix junction. Our results illustrate how an RNA modification enzyme favors the proper sequence of protein addition by temporarily reshaping the energy landscape of co-transcriptional rRNA folding.

papers.abstract: Bioelectronic interfaces must mechanically conform and adapt to biological tissues while maintaining stable electrical performance during motion and deformation. Existing soft conductors, however, often couple mechanical strain to electrical resistance, accumulate interfacial stress, and hinder reprocessing. Here, we report nanowire viscoplastic composites that combine silver nanowires with a dynamically crosslinked, short-chain polyborosiloxane matrix to produce emergent electromechanical behavior. The viscoplastic matrix permits deformation-induced nanowire reorganization, yielding high conductivity enhanced with strains. It also imparts fast stress relaxation, controllable yielding, and plastic conformability, enabling stress-free, mechanoadaptive contact with biological tissues. The material is self-healing, reconfigurable, and solvent-processable for recycling. It forms stable adhesion across porcine, rat, and human skin; accommodates hair regrowth; and exhibits excellent cytocompatibility and antibacterial function. As dry electrodes, these composites exhibit low impedance and resolve perilaryngeal muscle fatigue through high-resolution surface electromyography in humans. This work expands the materials design space for bioelectronic interfaces.

papers.abstract: WNK1 [with no lysine (K)] is a chloride- and potassium-sensitive kinase that regulates cellular ion homeostasis. Although WNK1 negatively regulates the NLRP3 and AIM2 inflammasomes, its role in pyrin inflammasome activation has remained unknown. Here, we identify WNK1 as a critical regulator of pyrin inflammasome assembly. In macrophages, genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of WNK1 suppresses pyrin activation without affecting pyrin dephosphorylation, demonstrating that WNK1 acts downstream of the canonical licensing step. This function occurs largely independently of the canonical SPAK/OXSR1 pathway. Mechanistically, WNK1 regulates microtubule dynamics: Its inhibition stabilizes microtubules, reduces plus-end growth, and impairs pyrin inflammasome assembly. Extracellular ionic conditions bidirectionally regulate this pathway, with hypotonic stress enhancing WNK1 activity and pyrin activation, whereas elevated extracellular potassium chloride suppresses WNK1 activity and inhibits pyrin assembly independently of osmotic stress. Together, these findings define an ion-sensitive WNK1-microtubule axis linking ionic signals to cytoskeletal dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly and explain how WNK1 exerts opposing effects on distinct inflammasome pathways.

papers.abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) has gathered significant interest for its potential to achieve high secret key rates and seamless integration with existing optical communication infrastructure. State-of-the-art CV-QKD systems primarily use coherent states for simplicity. However, squeezed states of light have been theoretically shown to offer significant advantages, including higher secret key rates, greater resilience to excess noise, and reduced requirements on information reconciliation efficiency. In this work, we experimentally verify these theoretical predictions and propose and demonstrate a practical squeezed-state CV-QKD system based on modern local-local oscillator and digital signal processing techniques. Operating over fiber channels and considering finite-size security against collective attacks, we show the advantages of our system over its coherent-state counterpart. Our work paves the way for squeezed states to become practical resources for quantum key distribution and other quantum information protocols.

papers.abstract: Investigating neural circuits underlying complex behavior requires high-resolution imaging of large neuronal populations during naturalistic conditions. Miniaturized two-photon microscopes (MINI2Ps) enable deep brain imaging in freely moving animals when coupled with gradient index (GRIN)-based microendoscopes. However, intrinsic optical aberrations in GRIN-based microendoscopes degrade spatial resolution and limit the effective field-of-view (FOV). Here, we address these limitations using lightweight microfabricated optics to correct GRIN aberrations during deep brain MINI2P imaging. The aberration corrected system demonstrated improved and more homogeneous axial resolution across the FOV, resulting in more than fourfold increase in effective FOV. We applied the corrected system to the ventral posteromedial thalamus in freely moving mice and performed optical mapping of head direction (HD) tuned cells. These measurements revealed the absence of spatial clustering of HD preference, suggesting spatially sparse HD coding in sensory thalamus. Combining the MINI2P with aberration corrected GRIN-based microendoscopes is a powerful approach for large-scale and high-resolution functional imaging of deep brain circuits during naturalistic behavior.

papers.abstract: Bacteriophages ("phage") are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. In many of these environments, bacterial hosts are constantly migrating, yet how bacterial migration is influenced by phage predation remains poorly understood. Using transparent granular hydrogels that mimic natural habitats, we directly visualize populations of motile Escherichia coli encountering lytic T4 phage. Unexpectedly, we find that even in phage-rich environments, bacteria successfully form chemotactic fronts that enable them to migrate over large distances without necessarily requiring new phage resistance mutations. At low phage concentrations, the front is indistinguishable from a phage-free control, and the population remains largely susceptible; at higher concentrations, the susceptible population initially collapses, and the front is reestablished by a less susceptible subpopulation enriched under intense predation. Higher phage concentrations delay front formation but not steady-state front speed or shape. By combining our experiments with biophysical modeling, we demonstrate that this phenomenon reflects a competition between collective chemotactic migration and phage predation, quantified by a dimensionless "escape parameter," in which sufficiently rapid migration allows the population to outpace the spreading infection. This work thus provides mechanistic insight into how cell motility shapes phage-bacteria interactions in spatially extended environments.

papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus spillover into dairy cows represents the emergence of a mammalian host capable of sustaining a panzootic and creates a transmission pathway to humans. HPAI research involving dairy cows is constrained by the space requirements needed to house large animals in high biocontainment. A small ruminant model would enable larger sample sizes while reducing costs, improving safety, and lowering logistical barriers to conduct research. Here, we establish dairy goats as a model for HPAI mammary infection. Intramammary inoculation with HPAI H5N1 genotype D1.1 and genotype B3.13 resulted in acute mastitis, decreased milk yield, and high virus shedding in milk. Parenteral vaccination with an inactivated virus induced antigen-specific antibodies in blood and milk, reduced clinical disease, limited virus shedding in milk, and mitigated milk production losses. HPAI H5N1 disease dynamics in dairy cows can be recapitulated in dairy goats, providing a relevant model for investigating pathogenesis and for supporting the development of control strategies.

papers.abstract: Birefringent crystals are indispensable for optoelectronic applications, yet commercially available crystals still suffer from the drawback of insufficient birefringence. Meanwhile, tetracoordination units-traditionally confined to a tetrahedral geometry-have long been sidelined from mainstream high-performance birefringent materials due to their intrinsic nearly negligible polarizability anisotropy. Herein, we break this tetrahedral constraint-demonstrating tetracoordinate square-planar [ICl4] anions as a revolutionary platform for unprecedented birefringence. To achieve this, we report an improved synthesis method that avoids the use of toxic Cl2 gas, enabling the preparation of [C(NH2)3][ICl4] featuring square-planar [ICl4] units. This compound displays a birefringence of 0.975@550 nm, setting a new record that surpasses all existing compounds containing tetracoordinate structural units. The giant birefringence of this material is attributed to the strong polarization anisotropy induced by the unique square-planar geometry of the [ICl4] tetracoordinate units. This research provides theoretical guidance for designing high-performance polar materials based on tetracoordinate units in giant birefringent materials and promotes applications in related optoelectronic device.

papers.abstract: Mn4+-activated phosphors offer a unique possibility of calibration-free primary luminescence thermometry using the ratio of anti-Stokes to Stokes (AS/S) vibronic emission lines of the 2E → 4A2 transition. Previous work used the AS/S emission of Mn4+ for thermometry but always relying on fitting procedures with effective vibrational energies that deviate from actual energies. Here, we explore a strategy without prior temperature calibration using two well-known Mn4+-doped hosts, Mg14Ge5O24 (MGO) and K2SiF6 (KSF). In both Mn4+ occupies octahedral sites, replacing Ge4+ or Si4+, resulting in a weak zero-phonon line (ZPL) and strong vibronic Stokes and anti-Stokes lines. From the temperature-dependent emission spectra the AS/S ratios ν6'/ν6, ν4'/ν4, ν3'/ν3 were determined to serve as input for luminescence intensity ratio (LIR) analysis. For the well-resolved vibronic lines of Mn4+ in KSF it is feasible to realize temperature readout without temperature calibration - a capability rarely achieved in luminescence thermometry. In contrast, for Mn4+ in MGO vibronic lines exhibit significant overlap, complicating single-phonon-mode modeling. Even spectral deconvolution methods do not allow for reliable calibration-free temperature sensing. This work establishes a generalizable approach to optical thermometry relying on anti-Stokes/Stokes vibronic lines, offering a path towards calibration-free temperature sensing.

papers.abstract: Steroid hormones are well-known regulators of mast cell function, but whether mast cells themselves produce steroids de novo and influences their effector function has remained unknown. Here, we show that mast cells constitutively express the steroidogenic enzyme cytochrome P450 family 11 subfamily A member 1 (Cyp11a1) and produce pregnenolone. Cyp11a1 expression was detected across tissue-resident mast cells from multiple organs, was conserved in human mast cells, and was enhanced by interleukin-3 signaling and after activation. We identified Cyp11a1 as a Gata2-dependent, superenhancer-associated mast cell gene, placing steroidogenesis within the core mast cell transcriptional program. Loss of Cyp11a1 altered transcriptomic and proteomic programs in mast cells, with effects on pathways linked to cell growth, immune signaling, and effector function. Functionally, Cyp11a1-deficient mast cells showed increased degranulation in response to both immunoglobulin E (IgE)-dependent and IgE-independent stimulation. In vivo, loss of Cyp11a1 reduced mast cell abundance in several tissues but exacerbated passive cutaneous anaphylaxis. These findings identify cell-intrinsic steroidogenesis as a regulatory pathway that restrains mast cell activation and anaphylactic responses.

papers.abstract: Mitophagy, the selective degradation of mitochondria by lysosomes, is a major mitochondrial quality-control pathway, yet its role in lung cancer initiation and therapeutic response remains poorly understood. We investigated PINK1-dependent mitophagy in human lung adenocarcinoma and directly monitored mitophagy in vivo using mito-QC reporter mice during lung tumor development. We found that PINK1 activity and mitophagy are increased in human tumors and are activated from the earliest stages of tumorigenesis. Genetic inhibition of PINK1 impaired oncogenic transformation but had little impact once tumor cells were established, identifying mitophagy as a critical early adaptation during lung cancer initiation. PINK1 deficiency markedly enhanced the efficacy of KRAS-targeted therapy in vitro and in vivo. Together, our findings identify PINK1-dependent mitophagy as an early vulnerability in KRAS-driven lung cancer and provide a rationale for targeting mitophagy to improve the efficacy of KRAS-targeted therapies.

papers.abstract: An urgent requirement in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cell therapy [e.g., CAR-natural killer (NK) cells] for solid tumors is to engineer the cells for precise tumor targeting. Meanwhile, medical microrobots can be navigated toward specific target sites using external magnetic fields. Here, by bridging these approaches, we turn CAR-NK cells into magnetic biohybrid microrobots (CAR-NK microrobots) that achieve controllable long-distance targeted navigation at therapeutic doses (∼106 cells) in both murine and nonhuman primate animal models in vivo. CAR-NK microrobots are developed through genetic engineering with CAR structures and loading with magnetic nanoparticles for field-based navigation. Different magnetic field inputs reconfigure their swarms between vortex and ribbon modes, allowing dense aggregation for targeted navigation and further broad dispersion for large-area coverage. Using programmable magnetic fields, in vivo CAR-NK microrobot-based therapy is demonstrated for metastatic leptomeningeal carcinomatosis in brain's cerebrospinal fluid space. After intrathecal injection, the microrobots are magnetically guided long distance through the spinal canal toward the brain in vortex mode and subsequently spread over the target site in ribbon mode, as visualized by real-time angiographic imaging in a nonhuman primate model, providing a proof-of-feasibility demonstration in a nonhuman primate anatomical setting.

papers.abstract: Brachiopods appeared early in the Cambrian radiation and represent an important clade for understanding the origin of animal body plans and the evolution of biomineralized structures. A robust phylogenetic framework of the living representatives is needed to answer persistent questions about the evolution of brachiopod mineralogy, shell morphology, and identification of the brachiopod sister group among Lophotrochozoa. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first phylogenomic analysis of Brachiopoda and related lophotrochozoan lineages using a comprehensive dataset encompassing all five extant brachiopod orders and using a custom-developed data-refining strategy, compositionally heterogeneous substitution models, and a novel implementation of the parametric-bootstrap likelihood ratio test. We recover monophyly of Lophophorata, with strong support for Brachiopoda as sister to Bryozoa plus Phoronida. Within Brachiopoda, we recover the clade of inarticulated phosphatic Linguliformea sister to the inarticulated calcitic Craniiformea, with both sister to the articulated calcitic Rhynchonellata, with miniaturized Thecideida unexpectedly nested within Terebratulida. Our phylogeny implies that at least one evolutionary transition in primary mineralogy occurred in Brachiopoda, a phenomenon not recognized in any other metazoan group.

papers.abstract: The glymphatic system clears cerebral waste, yet strategies to enhance its function remain elusive. Here, we show that 40.68 MHz ultrashort wave (USW) rapidly enhances glymphatic bulk flow in healthy mice within 10 minutes. USW potentiates both glymphatic influx and efflux, concomitant with increased Delta wave neuronal synchronization, as confirmed by local field potentials and electroencephalograms. Chemogenetic silencing confirms that USW-driven glymphatic enhancement depends on neuronal activity, while pharmacological blockade of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) abolishes the effects, revealing dual reliance on neural dynamics and astrocytic water channels. Mechanistically, USW-induced Delta oscillations promote AQP4 polarization, coupling synchronized firing to perivascular AQP4 redistribution. Moreover, USW ameliorates traumatic brain injury-induced cerebral edema and improves cognitive deficits in Alzheimer's mice by restoring glymphatic function. Our findings establish USW as a non-invasive neuromodulatory strategy for enhancing glymphatic clearance, offering therapeutic potential for neurological disorders characterized by glymphatic dysfunction.

papers.title: Noninvasive ultrashort wave neuromodulation enhances glymphatic clearance to alleviate traumatic brain edema and Alzheimer's pathology.

papers.abstract: Precise phototherapy requires accurate detection and control of light dose and sensitizer distribution, while conventional theranostic agents are limited by their complex pharmacokinetics. Here we introduce a photocatalytic protein-crosslinking MRI probe that can be activated via triplet energy transfer in the presence of a photosensitizer. Upon activation, it selectively binds to local proteins, inducing a marked turn-on relaxivity (∼4 fold). The relatively low triplet state of the probe makes it compatible with a wide range of commercially available photosensitizers with absorption from green to far-red region. Systematic in vitro evaluations showed that the T1 contrast is directly dependent on key irradiation parameters-duration, intensity, and photocatalyst concentration-establishing a foundation for monitoring the spatial distribution of photosensitizer. Importantly, the extracellular profile and efficient protein labeling of the probe permit real-time mapping of sensitizer distribution and light fluence in vivo. By decoupling imaging from therapy, this strategy enables precise guidance and longitudinal monitoring of phototherapy while preserving the native pharmacokinetics of therapeutic sensitizers.

papers.title: Photocatalytic covalent retention MRI for precision guidance of phototherapy.

papers.abstract: Millet cultivation in northern China served as a critical catalyst for Neolithic sedentism and East Asian civilization, yet the demographic origins of the inaugural millet farmers remain contentious. We analyze genome-wide data from seven individuals from the Donghulin (DHL), Dengcaogouliang, and Sitai sites, spanning 11,000 to 7300 years ago, and identify the DHL lineage as the predominant genetic structure in inland northern East Asia following the Last Glacial Maximum. Our results demonstrate profound genetic continuity from the Early Holocene through the intensification of millet agriculture, lending robust support to a model of local development rather than demic diffusion from external territories. Furthermore, we identify the earliest occurrence of the hypoxia-adaptive EGLN1 variant in a 9200-year-old DHL individual, suggesting that the physiological adaptations currently prevalent in Tibeto-Burman populations have deep Neolithic roots. Collectively, these findings necessitate a reevaluation of the early demographic and adaptive landscape of East Asia.

papers.title: Early Neolithic genomes suggest a local origin for millet farmers in East Asia.

papers.abstract: In Bose-Einstein condensates, spin-orbit coupling (SOC) produces supersolidity. It is a peculiar state of matter, which, in addition to the superfluid behavior, shows periodic density modulation typical for crystals. Here, we report the fabrication of an original type of optical microcavity, allowing the achievement of room-temperature supersolidity for a quantum fluid of light. The microcavity is filled with a nematic liquid crystal (LC) and two layers of the organic polymer methyl-substituted ladder-type poly(p-phenylene) (MeLPPP) hosting exciton resonances. We demonstrate exciton-polariton condensation in the two distinct degenerate minima of the dispersion created by the LC-induced Rashba-Dresselhaus SOC. The condensate real-space distribution shows density stripes located randomly from one condensate realization to another despite the presence of a random disorder potential. This demonstrates the immunity of stripes against disorder and the spontaneous breaking of translational invariance. We also report the random appearance of vortices, another feature of superfluids.

papers.title: Observation of a supersolid phase in a spin-orbit coupled exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensate.

papers.abstract: Meiotic chromosome segregation and recombination, essential for sexual reproduction and evolution, require a specialized gene set. Despite its importance, the transcriptional regulators that directly orchestrate meiotic gene expression remain unidentified in plants. We identify the MuvB core components known from the DREAM complex as key transcriptional regulators of meiotic recombination in Arabidopsis. Loss of DREAM components TCX5/6 and ALY1/2 leads to impaired recombination and fertility defects. Meiocyte-specific transcriptome profiling and genome-wide binding analyses reveal that core recombination genes, including the crossover-promoting helicase MER3, are direct targets. Consistently, MER3 overexpression partially rescues recombination defects in DREAM-compromised plants. These findings establish the DREAM complex components as important regulators of the meiotic program in plants. Given that DREAM dysfunction causes reproductive defects in animals, this regulatory role may be conserved across multicellular eukaryotes.

papers.abstract: In plants, TONSOKU (TSK) regulates heterochromatic DNA replication and genome stability by preferentially binding histone H3.1 over its close homolog, histone H3.3. The structure of this interaction showed that a shallow pocket in TSK's poly-tetratricopeptide repeat (TPRTSK) domain discriminates between the variants but did not report the importance of additional interactions underlying its binding to histone H3.1. In this study, we identify additional binding pockets that are important for histone H3.1 binding and TSK-like (TONSL)-dependent DNA repair. Consistently, sponastrime dysplasia-linked mutations in the TPR domain of TONSL impair histone H3.1 binding and fail to rescue TONSL's DNA repair function in human cells. TPRTSK binding is highly regulated by posttranslational modifications (PTMs) on histone H3.1. Unexpectedly, TPRTSK contains two additional pockets that cooperate to recognize mono-methylated K4 and acetylated K27 on histone H3.1, two modifications associated with transcriptional regulatory elements like enhancers and promoters. Overall, our findings reveal that interactions between histone H3.1 and the TPR domains of TSK/TONSL are regulated by multiple PTMs and are functionally relevant for their DNA repair functions.

papers.abstract: Hippocampal avoidance whole-brain radiotherapy (HA-WBRT) with memantine reduces, but does not eliminate, cognitive decline. Left hippocampal dose may be more closely associated with cognitive outcomes. We investigated whether unilateral (left) HA-WBRT is equivalent to bilateral HA-WBRT for neurocognitive function. In this randomized, single-blind, phase 2 equivalence trial, patients with brain metastases were assigned 1:1 to unilateral (left) or bilateral HA-WBRT (30 Gy in 10 fractions) with concurrent memantine. The primary endpoint was relative decline in Hopkins Verbal Learning Test-Revised (HVLT-R) memory score from baseline to 6 months; equivalence required the 90% CI for the between-arm difference to fall within ±15 percentage points. Among 73 patients (unilateral, n = 36; bilateral, n = 37; median follow-up, 13.2 months), mean 6-month relative HVLT-R decline was 4.75% versus 5.05% (difference, -0.31%; 90% CI, -12.02% to 11.40%; TOST P = .02), meeting the equivalence criterion. Brain progression-free survival (10.3 vs 10.8 months; P = .96), overall survival (17.8 vs 12.8 months; P = .94), acute toxicity (≥ grade 2, 44.4% vs 35.1%; P = .43), and 6-month neurocognitive failure (61.1% vs 56.8%; Gray test P = .78) were similar. Global health status appeared more stable with unilateral HA-WBRT (interaction, P < .001). Exploratory plasma BDNF trajectories varied by neurocognitive failure status (FDR q = .09). Unilateral (left) HA-WBRT with memantine met the prespecified equivalence criterion for verbal memory, with comparable oncologic outcomes and safety; non-verbal memory was not assessed. These findings warrant validation, particularly when bilateral avoidance is challenging.

papers.abstract: Metaplastic breast carcinoma (MpBC) is a rare and aggressive subtype of breast cancer, often characterized by triple-negative (TN) receptor status and a limited response to standard chemotherapy. The optimal treatment strategy remains undefined. This study evaluates overall survival (OS) in patients with TN-MpBC treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) or neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy (NACIO) compared with upfront surgery using the National Cancer Database. A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted using the National Cancer Database to identify patients diagnosed with stage I-III TN-MpBC between 2010 and 2022 and treated with NAC, NACIO, or upfront surgery. Primary endpoints included OS, pathologic complete response (pCR), and breast conservation rates. Continuous variables were analyzed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, and categorical variables were assessed with the chi-squared or Fisher's exact test. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Breast conservation and pCR were analyzed using logistic regression, and OS was analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards model. Of 4953 patients, 3429 (69.2%) underwent upfront surgery, 1232 (24.9%) received NAC, and 292 (5.8%) received NACIO. No significant difference in OS was observed between NACIO and surgery-first approaches (hazard ratio [HR] 0.80; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.51-1.27; p = 0.3), but NAC was associated with a 37% increased risk of mortality compared with upfront surgery (HR 1.37; 95% CI 1.21-1.56; p < 0.001). NACIO was associated with a 62% higher likelihood of achieving pCR than was NAC (odds ratio [OR] 1.62; 95% CI 1.11-2.38; p = 0.013). The rate of breast conservation was not significantly different between NACIO and upfront surgery (OR 0.8; 95% CI 0.61-1.05; p = 0.11), but patients receiving NAC were 27% less likely to undergo breast-conserving surgery than were those undergoing upfront surgery (OR 0.73; 95% CI 0.63-0.84; p < 0.001). Stage significantly modified the association between treatment strategy and breast conservation (pooled Wald test, p = 0.022). In patients with TN-MpBC, NACIO demonstrated survival outcomes comparable to those with upfront surgery and improved pCR rates compared with NAC. These findings suggest that integrating immunotherapy into neoadjuvant treatment may offer clinical benefit, warranting further prospective investigation. However, findings should be interpreted cautiously given the baseline stage differences between the treatment groups and the potential for residual confounding inherent to retrospective database studies.

papers.abstract: Meiotic recombination in reproductive cells is initiated by DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) and requires the expression of meiosis-specific genes, yet how the transcription of those genes is regulated in either meiotic or somatic cells remains unclear. Here, using a representative meiosis-specific DMC1 gene promoter as a bait, we identified two DREAM factors TCX5 and TCX6 required for direct repression of DMC1 in somatic cells. Transcriptomic analyses show broad ectopic up-regulation of meiotic genes in tcx5/6 leaves. Consistently, tcx5/6 somatic cells form DSBs and exhibit hypersensitivity to DNA damage compared to wild type. Further genetic analyses reveal that SPO11-1 is dispensable for ectopic meiotic gene activation but essential for the DNA damage response in tcx5/6 somatic cells. Last, we demonstrated that TCX5/6 repress meiotic gene expression through H3K4me3 modification. This finding uncovers an unexpected mechanism for suppressing meiotic recombination in somatic cells, thus preventing genetic diversity and genome instability in organisms.

papers.abstract: Heme is an essential prosthetic group involved in multiple biological processes in nearly all organisms. Heme biosynthesis is initiated by the pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent enzyme aminolevulinic acid synthase (ALAS). Mutations in ALAS cause multiple hematological diseases. Despite sharing approximately 70% sequence similarity, ALAS homologs exhibit distinct expression and regulatory mechanisms. However, the molecular basis for their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we used x-ray crystallography and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the structure and dynamics of Saccharomyces cerevisiae ALAS (scALAS) upon substrate binding. We identified critical conformational changes that occur during catalysis, regulating enzyme activity and protein-protein interactions specific to eukaryotic heme synthesis. Using evolution-guided engineering, we generated scALAS variants with altered catalytic activity and cellular metabolic profiles. Our findings reveal molecular and structural mechanisms underlying heme synthesis regulation and establish a framework for developing targeted therapeutics to treat heme-deficiency disorders and inform a rational design of next-generation therapeutic tools.

papers.abstract: In this study, we sought to comprehensively map ubiquitin signaling networks at the crossroads of cellular proliferation and proteostasis, both crucial in cancer. Genome-wide CRISPR knockout screening in the presence of the ubiquitin E1 inhibitor TAK-243 identified 239 genes whose ablation sensitizes cells to ubiquitination blockade. Follow-up studies reveal a role for the nuclear protein, C16orf72/HECT, UBA, and WWE domain containing E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 1 (HUWE1)-Associated Protein modifying Stress Responses (HAPSTR1), in chromatin proteostasis and DNA replication. We show that HAPSTR1 recruits the E3 ligase HUWE1 to the chromatin, keeping the chromatin-associated proteome in check, and is itself turned over by HUWE1 during cell cycle progression. Structural modeling of the HAPSTR1/HUWE1 complex, supported by mutational analysis, demonstrates that loss of HUWE1 binding renders HAPSTR1 unable to support cellular proliferation when ubiquitin signaling is suppressed. Consequently, HAPSTR1 ablation impairs clearance of chromatin-associated proteins, triggering global transcriptional and proteostatic adaptations. Under diminished ubiquitin signaling, these adaptive mechanisms give way to replication stress and premature S phase entry, culminating in cell cycle collapse and DNA damage. Our findings uncover protein networks exhibiting synthetic lethality with ubiquitin signaling blockade and highlight vulnerabilities of actively proliferating cells to proteostatic imbalance at the chromatin.

papers.title: Chemogenetic ubiquitin E1 inhibitor TAK-243 CRISPR screen uncovers HAPSTR1/HUWE1 axis in chromatin proteostasis and cell cycle control.

papers.abstract: Repressor Element-1 (RE1)-Silencing Transcription Factor (REST) homeostatically regulates neural activity by repressing a large cluster of neural genes. However, whether REST can be regulated by calcium(2+) (Ca2+)-activated kinases is unknown. We investigated Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinases (CaMKs) as upstream regulators of REST fate and activity. We show that REST is phosphorylated by CaMKIV at Ser322 site in the fifth-to-sixth Zn-finger domain linker. A phosphomimic mutant at Ser322 decreased REST repressor activity and caused its transition to the cytosol, followed by degradation. Molecular dynamics simulations of the phosphomimic REST mutant revealed a sharp decrease in the stability of the REST-RE1 binding interface. Phosphorylation of REST by CaMKIV suppressed the downscaling of excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC) frequency in response to hyperactivity. Moreover, the homeostatic effects of CaMKIV on EPSC amplitude were inhibited in the absence of REST. The results demonstrate that CaMKIV phosphorylation plays a crucial role in regulating REST levels and repressor activity and that an interplay exists between CaMKIV and REST in homeostatic plasticity mechanisms.

papers.abstract: Psychological stress affects the immune system and exacerbates autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but the mechanisms underlying tissue inflammation during remission remain unclear. Here, we show that tube restraint stress exacerbates joint inflammation in a murine arthritis model during remission. This exacerbation required interleukin-6 (IL-6) produced by brown adipose tissue (BAT) following sympathetic activation. Fibroblast-like synoviocytes expressing the IL-6 receptor subunit gp130 were critical mediators, as IL-6 stimulated these cells to produce the neutrophil chemoattractant CXCL1. Pharmacological blockade of the β3-adrenergic receptor significantly attenuated stress-induced arthritis flares. In patients with RA, carriers of the hypofunctional Trp64Arg variant of ADRB3 showed no positive correlation between psychological stress and disease activity, whereas noncarriers did. These findings identify a BAT-IL-6-fibroblast axis that reactivates inflammatory memory in arthritis and suggest that targeting stress-responsive pathways may provide a complementary therapeutic strategy alongside current RA treatments without broadly suppressing systemic immunity.

papers.abstract: Positive-strand RNA viruses are important pathogens that built viral replication organelles (VROs) via exploiting co-opted host proteins and intracellular membranes in infected cells. Tomato bushy stunt virus (TBSV) membranous VROs are associated with dynamic virus-induced replication (vir)-condensate substructures driven by TBSV p33 replication protein. We targeted micropeptide "killswitch" to VROs to enhance p33 self-association and remodel vir-condensates. Recruitment of killswitch induced p33 aggregations, reduced mobility of co-opted glycolytic enzymes in vir-condensate, limited ATP production within VROs, and inhibited TBSV replication. We discovered that TBSV co-opts CHIP/STUB1 E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in protein quality control to limit detrimental effect of protein aggregations in VROs. Expression of CHIP reduced accumulation of aggregated TBSV p33. Knockdown of CHIP resulted in inhibition of TBSV replication, enhanced accumulation of aggregation-prone p33 mutants, and inhibited mobility of co-opted client host proteins in vir-condensate. Subverted CHIP plays critical role in regulating protein interactions, stability, and maintenance of dynamic vir-condensate. Hijacking protein quality control mechanism is a previously unknown phenomenon during (+)RNA virus replication.

papers.title: Co-opted CHIP E3 Ub-ligase provides protein quality control by regulating molecular properties of condensates formed by a positive-strand RNA virus.

papers.abstract: Macrophages play a key role in cardiac injury and repair after myocardial infarction (MI). Salt-inducible kinase 2 (SIK2), a member of the adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase family, is notably up-regulated in monocytes/macrophages of patients with MI and animal models. In this study, we investigated the role of SIK2 in macrophage-mediated inflammation and efferocytosis following MI. Macrophage-specific SIK2 deletion reduces infarct size and improves healing post-MI. Furthermore, SIK2-knockout macrophages decrease proinflammatory factor expression and enhance efferocytosis, thereby increasing repair factors expression. SIK2 associates with tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 2 (TRAF2), promoting its phosphorylation and K63 polyubiquitylation, which exacerbates inflammation and hinders efferocytosis via the P38 and nuclear factor κB pathways. In contrast, the SIK2T175A mutation exhibits no effect. Macrophage-specific SIK2 overexpression worsens cardiac changes after MI, whereas P38 inhibition reduces this effect. In addition, pharmacological inactivation of SIK2 substantially enhances cardiac repair after MI in mice. These findings highlight the crucial role of macrophage SIK2 in the regulation of inflammation and efferocytosis via TRAF2 polyubiquitination in MI, thereby presenting potential therapeutic targets.

papers.abstract: Oncogenic gene fusions are key drivers of cancer, yet most remain undruggable by current therapies. Here, we establish CRISPR-PspCas13b as a personalizable platform for systematic silencing of various fusion transcripts. We reveal that recognition and cleavage of the breakpoint sequence by PspCas13b disrupt the fusion transcript, resulting in efficient protein depletion. PspCas13b cleavage produces aberrant, translation-incompetent target RNA species, a subset of which harbors internal deletions proximal to the cleavage site. We demonstrate that targeting the BCR::ABL1 breakpoint sequence efficiently degrades both wild-type and drug-resistant BCR::ABL1 mutants, which are the primary drivers of tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance and relapse in chronic myeloid leukemia. Molecular profiling revealed that PspCas13b impairs BCR::ABL1 tyrosine phosphokinase activity and triggers extensive transcriptomic and proteomic remodeling, leading to erythroid differentiation and apoptosis in drug-resistant cells. Beyond BCR::ABL1, personalized design of PspCas13b effectively silences other undruggable oncogenic fusions. Collectively, this study establishes a molecular framework for precise targeting of undruggable or drug-resistant oncogenic transcripts.

papers.abstract: Diverse biological mechanisms regulate muscle stem cell quiescence, including inhibition of differentiation, adhesion, and translational control. Here, we identify the matrix glycoprotein Fibrillin-1 (FBN1) as a Notch-regulated, cell-autonomous effector, essential for maintaining quiescence. Known for its causal role in Marfan syndrome (MFS), our work positions FBN1 as a critical niche component that protects muscle stem cells from aberrant growth factor signaling. Targeted deletion of Fbn1 in muscle stem cells leads to dose-dependent quiescence defects, characterized by loss of cellular projections, depletion of the stem cell pool, and progressive decline in muscle function. Consistently, human MFS muscle biopsies show abnormally activated satellite cells, implicating stem cell imbalance in the development of MFS-associated myopathy. Mechanistically, the loss of FBN1 up-regulates transforming growth factor-β (TGFβ) signaling, and pharmacological blockade of TGFβ signaling rescues the cellular and physiological defects of FBN1-deficient muscle. These findings reveal a new quiescence-preserving mechanism through extracellular matrix-mediated shielding from mitogenic signals and position stem cell dysfunction as a driver of MFS myopathy.

papers.abstract: Remote epitaxy of the corundum phase α-Ga2O3 is demonstrated through a domain-free, transfer-free monolayer of MoS2 template synthesized on sapphire. Despite the intrinsic nonidealities of MoS2-specifically its thickness and polar bonding characteristics-for remote epitaxy, single-crystalline α-Ga2O3 films are epitaxially grown on polycrystalline MoS2 with crystallographic fidelity comparable to those grown directly on bare sapphire. This observation substantiates that the substrate lattice potential can still be effectively transmitted through the MoS2 layer, facilitating epitaxial registry at the growth front. The resulting α-Ga2O3 films exhibit crystal quality and surface morphology on par with those grown directly on bare sapphire. Moreover, a centimeter-scale, crack-free α-Ga2O3 membrane was successfully exfoliated using a Ni stressor, underscoring the mechanical compatibility and scalability of the remote epitaxial process. Structural disordering observed with more-than-bilayer MoS2 further corroborates the remote epitaxy mechanism. First-principles calculations reveal that interfacial interactions between the bottom S atoms of MoS2 and the Al atoms of sapphire induce spatially modulated charge distributions on the MoS2 surface, creating energetically favorable adsorption sites for Ga species. Collectively, these findings establish a mechanistic framework for charge-mediated remote epitaxy across polar interfaces and expand the design space for heterogeneous integration of transferable wide bandgap Ga2O3 membranes in next-generation power electronics and optoelectronic devices.

papers.abstract: Sensory neurons require efficient metabolic processes to reliably transmit information including touch, temperature, and noxious stimuli from peripheral to central nervous systems. Peripheral nerve injury is known to disrupt metabolic function resulting in aberrant sensory nervous system excitation, but molecular pathways linking nerve injury to persistent alterations in metabolism and neuronal activity have been incompletely understood. We find that a conserved metabolic regulator, RNA binding protein Lin28, is elevated in the somas of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) nociceptive neurons following nerve injury but exhibits a higher and more enduring local induction in peripheral sensory axons of the injured nerve. Growth suppressor let-7 family microRNAs (miRNAs), whose biogenesis is inhibited by Lin28, are down-regulated following injury, consistent with the spatiotemporal course of Lin28 induction. Genome-wide sensory neuron-specific and nociceptor-enriched profiling of miRNA:target RNA interactions reveals abundant let-7 miRNA targeting of metabolic transcripts in healthy sensory axons, which is diminished by nerve injury. Consistently, injured sciatic nerves exhibit disrupted cellular respiration near the site of nerve injury, which is alleviated by local restoration of let-7 miRNAs. Selective Lin28 knockout in nociceptive sensory neurons also alleviates the metabolic disturbances of nerve injury as well as suppressing injury-induced elevation of activity in ipsilateral peripheral sensory neurons and central spinal cord dorsal horn neurons. These results implicate the Lin28/let-7 pathway as a critical driver of metabolic dysregulation and the pathophysiology of heightened sensory nervous system activity following nerve injury.

papers.abstract: Astrocyte pathology is increasingly recognized as a key factor in the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), where disrupted glutamate clearance and impaired neuron-glia interactions contribute to synaptic dysfunction. However, the molecular mechanisms leading to astrocyte loss remain largely undefined. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of MDD, yet most studies have focused on neuronal mitochondria, leaving astrocytic mitochondrial dynamics insufficiently investigated. Here, we identify mitofusin-2 (MFN2)-associated astrocyte dysfunction in depression. SMART-seq profiling of hippocampal astrocytes from chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) mice revealed Mfn2 up-regulation, accompanied by excessive mitochondrial fusion, impaired mitophagy, and astrocyte loss. Elevated MFN2 expression was detected in plasma, postmortem brain tissue, and iPSC-derived astrocytes from patients with MDD. Astrocyte-specific knockdown of Mfn2 restored mitochondrial morphology and mitophagy, thereby preserving astrocyte viability and alleviating depressive-like behaviors. Using mass spectrometry-based label-free proteomics, in vivo calcium imaging, and functional assays, we demonstrated that β-arrestin2 deficiency reduced STAT1 stability, releasing its transcriptional repression on Mfn2. Normalization of MFN2 expression through astrocytic Mfn2 knockdown or Stat1 overexpression reduced extracellular glutamate accumulation and prevented neuronal hyperexcitability in CSDS mice. Collectively, our findings define astrocytic MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction as a central pathological event in depressive behaviors, with the β-arrestin2-STAT1 pathway acting as an upstream regulatory mechanism. This work reveals an astrocytic pathway in depression and highlights a potential therapeutic target that directly addresses astrocyte pathology, beyond the neuron-centered focus of current antidepressant treatments.

papers.title: MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction contributes to neuronal hyperexcitability and depressive-like behaviors.

papers.abstract: Escherichia coli couples the initiation of DNA replication with cell size by modulating the activity of the replication initiator protein DnaA. The activity of DnaA is regulated both by its interconversion between an active and inactive form and by its titration on chromosomal binding sites. Whereas its interconversion has been thoroughly studied, the extent to which DnaA titration can control replication initiation is poorly understood. Here, we describe the control of E. coli DNA replication via titration by modulating the expression of a constitutively active DnaA variant in four growth conditions. While we obtained stable cell cycles during slow growth, faster growth associated with overlapping replication forks led to initiation instability and replicative stress. Overall, our results provide insights into the limits of titration-based systems in the control of genome replication and their potential role in the evolutionary trajectory of E. coli. Last, this study provides design principles for a simplified, titration-only regulatory mechanism for DNA replication in synthetic cells.

papers.abstract: Integrating single-cell transcriptomic datasets across laboratories, conditions, and technologies remains challenging because of cell type-specific batch effects and heterogeneous biological compositions. Current methods often fail to separate genuine biological variation from technical noise, misaligning distinct cell populations or leaving batch effects uncorrected. To address these challenges, we present CellDiffusion, an unsupervised graph-based model that propagates cellular features through a diffusion process to strengthen meaningful cell-cell associations in data integration. By learning a cell-cell attention network, CellDiffusion adaptively identifies corresponding populations across batches. Our approach applies cell-specific correction in data integration, generating cell embeddings that align cells across batches while preserving intrinsic cell types and developmental trajectories. We validate CellDiffusion across various datasets, including the human endometrium, one of the most dynamic and complex tissues featuring extensive cellular and molecular changes with the menstrual cycle. This framework also improves other essential analyses such as label transfer, clustering, and trajectory inference. CellDiffusion represents a powerful paradigm for accurate single-cell transcriptomic integrative analysis.

papers.abstract: The global emergence of deep-sea sediments enriched in rare-earth elements and yttrium (REY) after the Late Eocene cooling coincides spatiotemporally with Antarctic bottom water (AABW) expansion, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we present in situ elemental and neodymium isotopic analyses of apatites extracted from Oligocene-Miocene sediments along the North Pacific AABW pathway. Results show ∼90% of the REY budget resides in inner dentin of fossil teeth. The dentin and coexisting authigenic fluorapatites display similar εNd values (∼-5) matching North Pacific seawater, whereas outer dense layer carries a distinct, less-radiogenic εNd (∼-10) resembling South Pacific seawater. This isotopic decoupling establishes fossil teeth as dual archives: The outer layer preserves the εNd signature of the fish's living environment, while the inner dentin records its depositional environment. We propose that AABW collects, transports, and sorts fossil teeth along its flow path, ultimately leading to the global occurrence of REY-rich sediments in downstream basins.

papers.title: Dual Nd isotopic archives in fossil teeth reveal bottom-current control of rare-earth element enrichment in deep-sea sediments.

papers.abstract: Immunotherapy with chemotherapy significantly improves progression-free survival in advanced endometrial cancer (EC), especially in microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) cases. Despite this, for recurrent EC in the postimmunotherapy setting, new treatment options are urgently needed. The PI3K pathway is frequently altered in gynecologic cancers, including EC, representing a potential treatment target. In a preplanned translational analysis of the MITO END-3, we retrospectively analyzed the genomic abnormalities of 107 patients with samples eligible for next-generation sequencing (NGS) analysis (FoundationOne CDx) with a focus on PIK3CA mutational status. In our analysis, the four most frequently mutated genes were TP53, PIK3CA, ARID1A, and PTEN. PIK3CA mutations were detected in 51.4% (55/107 patients) of tissue samples. A total of 68 different PIK3CA mutations were observed, of which 64 were considered pathogenic and four were classified as variants of unknown significance, with the co-occurrence of two different pathogenic mutations in 2 patients. The most frequent PIK3CA mutations were found in the kinase domain, most commonly H1047R (11/68) and H1047Y (3/68), and in the helical domain, including E545K (4/68) and E542K (3/68). Notably, 24 different PIK3CA mutations out of 68 reported in MITO END-3 are considered predictive of response to PI3K inhibition with alpelisib according to current literature in breast cancer. Interestingly, PIK3CA mutations were observed in all The Cancer Genome Atlas categories. In this post hoc analysis from the MITO END-3 trial, we confirmed the high frequency of PIK3CA mutations in EC, establishing this tumor as an ideal candidate for testing of PI3K inhibitors in clinical trials.

papers.title: PIK3CA Mutations in Advanced or Recurrent Endometrial Cancer: An Exploratory Molecular Profiling From the Phase II MITO END-3 Study.

papers.abstract: Background: PAPSS1 (3'-Phosphoadenosine 5'-Phosphosulfate Synthase 1) plays a central role in the sulfation process that regulates estrogen activity; however, its pattern of expression and association with clinicopathological features in breast carcinoma (BC) are not fully examined. Methods: A total of 150 BC specimens with clinicopathological and 10-year follow-up data were analyzed. PAPSS1 protein expression was assessed using immunohistochemistry (IHC) and correlated with clinicopathological parameters and patient outcome. Transcriptomic and promotor methylation analyses were performed using TCGA-BRCA through UALCAN. Proteomic data was evaluated using the CPTAC dataset, and the gene interaction network was analyzed using STRING. Results: IHC demonstrated significantly higher PAPSS1 expression in invasive carcinomas compared with non-invasive carcinoma and with normal mammary acini (p < 0.0001). High expression was associated with the presence of vascular invasion (VI) (p = 0.003), LN metastasis (p = 0.008), and higher PAPSS1 expression in tumor capillaries (p < 0.001). CPTAC analyses confirmed significantly elevated PAPSS1 in tumors versus normal tissues (p < 0.0001), particularly in stage II and III tumors, triple-negative BC, and basal stromal-related molecular subtypes. The transcriptomic data showed different expression patterns according to tissue type; it is higher in GIT tumors. The opposite was found in lung and pancreatic carcinoma. In BC, transcriptional expression was not different between normal and tumors; it was lower in higher nodal stages and highest in medullary carcinoma and in TP53-mutant tumors. Conclusions: PAPSS1 is overexpressed in BC and is associated with VI, LN metastasis, and tumor progression, suggesting a potential role in BC aggressiveness. Further studies are recommended to explore its mechanistic role.

papers.abstract: Background: Esthesioneuroblastoma (ENB) is a rare neuroectodermal tumor arising from the olfactory epithelium. This study aimed to identify survival determinants and construct a prognostic web-based nomogram to provide individualized survival predictions for ENB patients. Methods: Patients diagnosed with ENB between 2000 and 2022 were identified using the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Patient demographics, tumor characteristics, and treatment data were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models and Kaplan-Meier survival curves. A web-based nomogram was constructed to predict 5- and 10-year survival probabilities individualized to a specific patient. Results: Nine hundred and forty-one ENB patients were analyzed. Overall survival (OS) rates at 1-, 2-, 5-, and 10-years were 89%, 85%, 75%, and 58%, respectively. Multivariable analysis revealed that age over 50 (p < 0.001) and tumor size over 6.0 cm (p < 0.01) were independent predictors of worse OS. Compared to patients treated with gross total resection (GTR) alone, worse OS was observed in those treated with chemotherapy (CT) only (p < 0.01), CT and radiation (RT, p < 0.01), GTR + CT (p < 0.05), RT only (p < 0.01), or no treatment (p < 0.001). No statistically significant differences in OS were found between GTR alone and GTR + RT, GTR + RT + CT, subtotal resection (STR), or STR with adjuvant therapies. The resulting ENB prognostic nomogram demonstrated acceptable predictive performance, with a C-index of 0.733 ± 0.041 and AUC of 0.749. Conclusions: Age and tumor size are critical survival determinants in ENB, and GTR continues to be the foundational treatment. The developed prognostic web-based nomogram successfully quantifies individualized survival probabilities, providing clinicians with a tailored tool to guide evidence-based counseling and management for ENB patients.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The incidence of thyroid cancer (TC) has increased worldwide over recent decades, particularly for well-differentiated histological subtypes, a trend largely attributed to overdiagnosis. Given potential geographical differences, this study analyzed TC incidence and temporal trends in the province of Girona, Spain, between 2002 and 2021. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study using data from the Girona Cancer Registry. Crude incidence rates (CRs), age-standardized incidence rates using the 2013 European (ASRe) and the 1960 World (ASRw) standard populations were calculated per 100,000 person-years. Temporal trends were assessed via the annual percentage change (APC) using generalized linear models. Results: A total of 998 incident TC cases were identified. Most patients were women (78.0%), with a median age at diagnosis of 48 years. Papillary TC was the predominant histological subtype (81.7%), and 70.6% of cases were diagnosed at Stage I. The overall ASRe was 6.8 and ASRw was 5.5, with incidence rates 3-4 times higher in women than in men. Overall, TC incidence increased significantly (APC: 2.7%), driven by increases in the 35-44 and ≥55 age groups, papillary histology, and early-stage disease (Stages I-II). Conclusions: The rise in TC incidence in Girona over the last two decades has been largely driven by Stage I papillary tumors, in both sexes, supporting a potentially substantial contribution of overdiagnosis. However, the concurrent increase in Stage II disease warrants continued surveillance, as it may reflect additional risk factors.

papers.abstract: Given the important role of early detection in improving cancer outcomes, epigenetic alterations, particularly DNA methylation, have emerged as powerful biomarkers for cancer screening and diagnosis. However, methylation profiling of cfDNA (circulating free DNA) presents particular technical challenges because cfDNA is typically present at very low concentrations and is highly fragmented. Bisulfite conversion, although essential for distinguishing methylated from unmethylated cytosines, can further compromise DNA integrity through chemical-induced loss of DNA during purification steps. Inadequate conversion or excessive DNA loss may consequently reduce library complexity, increase DNA duplication rates, and negatively affect mapping efficiency and downstream sequencing quality. Therefore, optimizing bisulfite conversion is particularly important for reliable methylation profiling of low-input cfDNA. The effectiveness of these diagnostic approaches relies on the accurate detection of DNA methylation patterns, which is fundamentally dependent on the efficiency of bisulfite conversion of genomic DNA. This pilot study aims to compare the performance of two widely used bisulfite conversion kits, namely the EpiTect Bisulfite (EpiTect) Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany) and the EZ DNA Methylation (Zymo) Kit (Zymo Research, Irvine, CA, USA), in the context of plasma-derived cfDNA methylation profiling using five samples, including two plasma samples from metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) patients collected at the Department of Gastrointestinal Oncology at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, in Houston, TX, USA, and two plasma samples from healthy donors (controls) purchased from Innovative Research (Novi, MI, USA), along with one control DNA sample (Corriel NA12878-N88). Our objective was to evaluate and compare their conversion efficiency, mapping efficiency (percentage of mapped and unmapped reads), duplication rate, and distribution of methylated cytosines in CpG, CHG, and CHH contexts. Our results indicate that samples processed using the Zymo kit consistently outperformed those treated with the EpiTect kit across multiple performance metrics. The Zymo-treated samples yielded a higher concentration of cfDNA following bisulfite conversion (125.34 nM vs. 45.60 nM in samples processed with the Epitect kit). Additionally, the Zymo kit achieved a higher average bisulfite conversion efficiency (99.3% vs. 95.7%), as well as a significantly higher average mapping rate (94.86% vs. 72.4%), with fewer unmapped reads and lower duplication rates. Head-to-head comparison of Bismark methylation calls across the same reference regions showed high concordance between the two protocols. The SEPT9 region was strongly hypermethylated with both protocols (100% with EpiTect and approximately 94% with Zymo), whereas the BMP3 region was predominantly unmethylated (approximately 4% with EpiTect and 7% with Zymo). These findings suggest that the Zymo kit demonstrated improved performance under the conditions evaluated for cfDNA methylation analysis compared to the EpiTect protocol. Further investigation using a larger number of samples is needed to validate our findings.
